newsitem.title: LEBANON: Palestinian camps strike against Israeli move.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian camps strike against Israeli move.

text.p: Palestinian refugees in south Lebanon observed on Saturday a general strike to protest Israel's building of a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Dozens of Palestinian guerrillas, brandishing AK-47 assault rifles and some carrying Palestinian flags, burned tires at the entrance of Ain el-Hilweh camp near the port of Sidon and al-Rashidiyeh camp further south.

Shops and businesses also shut down in three other camps in south Lebanon, heeding the strike call by Palestinian factions in the south, including loyalists to PLO leader Yasser Arafat and radical groups opposed to his 1993 peace deal with Israel.
Saturday's strike was to "express solidarity with the steadfast people inside Palestine and to assert the unity of the cause and fate", the Lebanon-based factions said in a statement.

Several Damascus-based radical Palestinian groups called last week on Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza Strip to carry out military attacks against Israel to confront its settlement building in Arab East Jerusalem.
The project has enraged Palestinians who regard East Jerusalem, capured by the Jewish state in 1967, as the capital of a future state.

"We announce our adherence to Jerusalem as an eternal capital for an independent Palestinian state," added the statement issued in Ain el-Hilweh, the biggest of 12 refugee camps across Lebanon and home to 75,000 Palestinian refugees.

On Friday, a Palestinian Moslem suicide bomber killed three people in a crowded cafe in Tel Aviv, in an attack that came amid heightened Israeli-Palestinian tension over the groundbreaking on Tuesday for the Jewish settlement.
